title: Sweet and Sour Pork with Rice

content.title: About
content.content: Sweet and sour pork with rice is a popular Asian dish featuring bite‑size pieces of pork coated in a thick sauce made from vinegar, sugar, soy sauce and tomato paste, served over steamed rice.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in China in the 19th century and quickly spread worldwide.
Traditional sauce uses pineapple juice, but many modern recipes rely on simple vinegar and sugar.
Original recipes call for pork tenderloin to keep the meat tender.
The sweet‑sour balance is considered appetizing and stimulates the palate.
It is a staple in fast‑food restaurants, yet homemade versions allow control over salt and sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Pork provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Thiamine, niacin and vitamin B6 in pork support energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Heme iron from pork is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Rice supplies carbohydrates
items.content: Steamed rice offers quick‑digesting carbs that replenish glycogen stores.

items.title: Vitamin C in the sauce
items.content: When tomato paste or pineapple is added, the sauce contributes vitamin C, which boosts immunity.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The sweet‑sour sauce can be sugar‑rich, which is a concern for diabetes or weight management.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Soy sauce adds significant salt, potentially raising blood pressure.

items.title: Fatty cuts
items.content: Some pork cuts are high in saturated fat; choosing leaner pieces is advisable.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: People allergic to soy should use alternative sauces.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cut pork into bite‑size pieces, stir‑fry until golden, add vegetables (bell pepper, carrot), pour a mixture of vinegar, sugar, soy sauce and tomato paste, simmer 5‑7 minutes. Cook rice separately until fluffy, then serve the pork over the rice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. Freeze up to 1 month, portioned appropriately.
